title: A method to improve cotton fiber length measurement for laboratory analysis
author: Morais, James, et al.

steps.title: Harvest seedcotton
steps.instruction: Harvest seedcotton by hand or using a cotton stripper harvester.

steps.title: Store harvest for equilibration
steps.instruction: Store the harvested seedcotton at 21 ± 1 °C and 55 ± 5 % relative humidity for at least seven days to allow equilibrium with ambient conditions.

steps.title: Clean stripper-harvested seedcotton
steps.instruction: If the seedcotton was harvested with a stripper, clean it to remove large sticks and burrs that could damage or hinder the laboratory‑scale gin.

steps.title: Feed seedcotton into saw‑gin
steps.instruction: Feed a laboratory‑scale saw‑gin equipped with 10–20 saws, delivering 4–6 g of seedcotton per saw per minute.

steps.title: Condition lint for testing
steps.instruction: Condition the lint at 21 ± 1 °C and 65 ± 2 % relative humidity for at least two days to reach equilibrium before analysis.

steps.title: Verify and adjust MDTA 3 settings
steps.instruction: Verify the settings of the Micro Dust and Trash Analyzer 3 (MDTA 3). If necessary, adjust the gauges between the feed roller and feed plate, the feed plate and opening roller, and the opening roller and trash knife to 0.1 mm.

steps.title: Power on MDTA 3 and set vacuum
steps.instruction: Turn on the MDTA 3 and set the vacuum to 3.5 mbar in the fiber channel and 2.5 mbar in the dust channel.

steps.title: Load lint onto MDTA 3 conveyor
steps.instruction: Evenly spread 4–5 g of the conditioned lint on the entire surface of the MDTA 3 conveyor belt and press the fibers at the end of the feed belt with the feed roller.

steps.title: Close rotor box and feed sample
steps.instruction: Close the rotor box and feed the lint sample into the machine.

steps.title: Recover and spread processed sliver
steps.instruction: Recover the sliver of processed fibers from the rotor ring box and spread it evenly on a flat surface.

steps.title: Sample processed lint portions
steps.instruction: From several parts of the sliver, sample small portions of processed lint, each up to 0.5 g.

steps.title: Repeat loading and sampling for replicates
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 8–11 for each laboratory replication of each sample that will be tested for fiber‑length quality.

steps.title: Hand‑draw uniform sliver
steps.instruction: Using each sampled mass of cleaned lint, hand‑draw a uniform sliver of fibers 25–30 cm in length.

steps.title: Analyze sliver with AFIS Pro 2
steps.instruction: Feed each sliver to an Advanced Fiber Information System (AFIS) Pro 2, testing 3 000 fibers per sliver.

steps.title: Retrieve analysis report
steps.instruction: Retrieve the AFIS report containing the fiber‑length quality data.
